names.name: Mahāmudrā (phyag rgya chen po, 'the great seal')
the nature of mind; mind-as-such (sems nyid)
co-emergent wisdom (lhan cig skyes pa'i ye shes)
ordinary mind (tha mal gyi shes pa)

descriptions: One's own mind, luminous (clear) and empty, unborn, beyond colour, shape and location, like space (Gaṅgā Mahāmudrā; Nāropa's Dṛṣṭisaṃkṣipta).

The union of clarity and emptiness, of appearance and emptiness, of bliss and emptiness — 'neither existent, for even the victors do not see it, nor non-existent, for it is the basis of saṃsāra and nirvāṇa' (3rd Karmapa's Aspiration Prayer).
Its emptiness is the dharmakāya, its unceasing radiance the nirmāṇakāya, their union great bliss the saṃbhogakāya (Karṇatantravajrapada).
The nature of thought is dharmakāya; appearances are the light of the dharmakāya.
negations: not an existent thing: 'even the victors do not see it'
not nothing: it is the basis of all saṃsāra and nirvāṇa
beyond speech, thought and expression; cannot be shown (Gaṅgā Mahāmudrā v1)
not a self (ātman) or a primordial nature (pradhāna) as the tīrthikas hold (Dṛṣṭisaṃkṣipta)
relation_to_self: The ultimate is one's own mind's nature, not something to be sought elsewhere; the 'self' grasped by beings is the delusion that obscures it; buddha-nature is present in all beings as the cause of awakening.
relation_to_world: Appearances are mind's own display, appearing yet empty like a moon in water; saṃsāra and nirvāṇa are that same mind obscured or freed of adventitious stains.
caveat: The Kagyu would reject reading 'mind's nature' as a single substance, a creator, or an eternal self in the Vedāntic sense: it is empty of any intrinsic existence and is realized, not posited. Vajradhara, from whom the lineage descends, is the dharmakāya in personal form for the lineage, not a creator. 'One taste' is the yogin's realization that appearances and mind are not two, not a monist ontology.

descriptions: The ground of purification is mind itself, clarity and emptiness inseparable; the purifier is the vajra yoga of Mahāmudrā; the purified are the adventitious stains; the fruit is the stainless dharmakāya (3rd Karmapa).
The eight consciousnesses, recognized, are the five wisdoms (Distinguishing Consciousness and Wisdom).
negations: neither existent nor non-existent; free of the extremes
relation_to_self: Buddha-nature is the beginningless element present in every being, obscured by adventitious stains.
relation_to_world: Appearances are mind; mind is empty; emptiness is not a blank but luminous.
caveat: The school holds two readings of how buddha-nature is empty — as empty of own-nature (the 8th Karmapa's Madhyamaka) or as empty only of what is other than it (the shentong reading of the 8th Situ and Jamgön Kongtrul) — not yet reconciled (dsp:rangtong-shentong).

names.name: the single intent (dgongs gcig) of the Buddha's word

descriptions: The whole of the Buddha's teaching has one intent, whose heart is Mahāmudrā; realized through the fivefold practice (bodhicitta, deity, guru, view, dedication).
negations: not reached by view alone without bodhicitta and devotion (the fivefold teaching)
relation_to_self: As in the Kagyu generally: the mind's own nature.
relation_to_world: The vows and practices of all vehicles are aspects of one intent rather than rival systems.
caveat: 'Single intent' concerns the unity of the Buddha's teaching, not a metaphysical monism.

names.name: Mahāmudrā, co-emergent union (lhan cig skyes sbyor)

descriptions: The co-emergent: mind-as-such is dharmakāya, appearances its light, thoughts its waves; adversity, illness and death, carried onto the path, are of one taste with it (the six equal tastes).
negations: not found by rejecting thoughts and afflictions
relation_to_world: Circumstances, including obstacles and death, are carried onto the path as one taste.

names.name: Mahāmudrā of the amulet box (phyag chen ga'u ma)
the four kāyas as self-liberated mind

descriptions: The mind's nature, left uncontrived, is self-liberated; its empty, clear and blissful aspects are the kāyas, 'enclosed together like the two halves of an amulet box' (the tradition's image for the inseparability of ground, path and fruit).
relation_to_world: Appearances are carried as the guru, the deity and illusion (the three integrations).
caveat: The amulet-box image and the 'three self-liberations' are Shangpa formulations known here only from memory; low confidence.
